_comment: ACCEPTED-RISK REGISTER. Every entry is a REVIEWED decision by Jake to ship with a known finding open - not a fix, and not a way to make a gate quiet. Validated by the check-security-baseline gate. Delete an entry the moment its finding is fixed.

accepted.summary: The web app is published ANYONE_ANONYMOUS executing as USER_DEPLOYING, so every unauthenticated caller reaches doPost/doGet running with the deploying user's Sheets, Drive and Gmail authority.
accepted.why_accepted: Structural, not an oversight. The callers are headless Playwright connectors on a scheduled task, not people: they hold no Google identity, so no access mode narrower than ANYONE_ANONYMOUS lets them POST at all, and the handler must write the owner's spreadsheet, which requires USER_DEPLOYING. The trust boundary is therefore enforced in CODE, and it was verified at the source on 2026-09-07 rather than assumed. doPost calls checkIngestToken_ as its FIRST statement - before validateIngest_ and before any write - using a PER-SOURCE token, so a token proves not just that the caller holds a secret but that it may claim the source it wrote in the body; it fails closed on unknown source, unset property, missing or wrong token, with no fallback to the doGet read secret. doGet calls checkReadToken_ before dispatching any fn. SCOPE OF THAT CLAIM (corrected 2026-09-16, see scope_correction): doPost and doGet are the entire anonymous WEB-APP surface - the GAS sources contain no HtmlService call and no google.script.run, so the app serves no HTML client and no other global is reachable through one. They are NOT the entire unauthenticated path into the Sheet; the Gmail-driven pulls are the other one, and they are credentialed separately (see scope_correction). The residual risk on THIS entry is an ingest token leaking, which is why they are per-source and revocable one connector at a time (docs/ingest-token-cutover.md). Revisit if the app ever starts serving an HtmlService page, if a new doPost/doGet branch is added ahead of its auth call, or if the /exec URL is shared beyond the connectors.

scope_correction.what_was_wrong: This entry previously read 'Those two are the entire anonymous surface.' That was false, and the High of the same 2026-09-10 audit is the proof: mayers.gs reached ingestSupplierRows - the same upsert doPost reaches only after checkIngestToken_ - from a Gmail search with no sender check at all, so anyone who knew the alias could overwrite a real invoice's amount in place. An auth-coverage tool cannot see that path by construction: there is no HTTP entry point to grade, the trigger is a scheduled pull, and the 'endpoint' is an email address.
scope_correction.why_the_decision_still_stands: The sentence was over-broad about SCOPE; it was not the reasoning the acceptance rests on. What justified accepting ANYONE_ANONYMOUS is that doPost/doGet each authenticate before any write, and that is unchanged and re-verified. The Gmail path was never covered by this entry and is not being accepted here - it is fixed: mayers.gs guards on MAYERS_ALLOWED_SENDERS (2b42bf1) and roastery_email.gs on ROASTERY_ALLOWED_SENDERS, both per-message, both fail-closed on an unset property.
scope_correction.how_to_keep_it_honest: Enumerate ingest paths by DATA FLOW - every writer that reaches a Sheet upsert - not by HTTP surface. As of 2026-09-16 the writers are: doPost (per-source ingest token) and doGet (read token, read-only) in Code.gs; the Gmail pulls mayers.gs and roastery_email.gs (per-message sender allowlist, fail-closed); square.gs, which writes Sales through appendSalesRow_ rather than upsertRows_ and so is easy to miss when grepping for the upsert; and orderapp.gs, shopspend.gs, recurring.gs, summary_audit.gs and summary_drift_repair.gs. Everything after the Gmail pulls runs on a time-based trigger as the owner and takes its input from an API key or from the owner own Sheet, so none of them has an anonymous caller to authenticate - that is the reason they need no credential, and it is a reason that stops being true the moment one of them accepts caller-supplied input. Adding a writer means adding its credential to this list or recording why it needs none.
